title: What If One Fish Was Dropped Into Africa's Biggest Lake?

scenes.text: What if one fish was added to Africa's biggest lake? It would be the fish nobody could stop.
In 1954, fisheries officers released Nile perch into Lake Victoria, hoping for a bigger catch.
Before it, the lake held upwards of 400 species of small cichlid fish, found nowhere else.
By the mid 1980s, those cichlids had vanished from the nets, and Tanzania's Nile perch catch jumped from 274 tonnes in 1981 to 123,879 tonnes by 1986.
Researchers estimate about 65 percent of the cichlid species were lost, and algae in the lake increased two to threefold.
The fishery got rich. But hundreds of species that evolved in one lake were gone, because of a fish nobody could take back.
